title: Phantom Blade Zero Collectibles - Every Type and What Each One Does
description: Phantom Blade Zero tracks collectibles per map with a total and a completion percentage. Three special items permanently raise Sha-chi, attack and health; bells clear map fog and serve as fast travel. Bilingual names included.

sections.title: How the Collection System Works
sections.content:
Phantom Blade Zero is built from large handcrafted maps joined seamlessly, in a wide-linear structure with light Metroidvania-style exploration and side content filling them out. The collectibles are what tell you whether you have actually walked one.

Community documentation describes three things the game does for you: it shows the total number of collectibles in the current map, it lists which specific pickups you have and have not taken, and the map screen displays a completion percentage. Locations that require a particular Phantom Edge to reach are marked on the map - so the game tells you a spot is gated rather than letting you wonder whether you missed it.

That last point changes how to read an incomplete map. A pinned location you cannot yet open is a promise, not a failure, and the percentage will keep it visible to you.

sections.title: Special Items: The Three Permanent Upgrades
sections.content:
The category the wiki lists as 特殊道具 is progression rather than loot. Three item types, each with a stated effect:

  • Sha-chi Amber shards (杀气琥珀碎片) - raise the cap on the Sha-chi bar, the resource that powers attacks, guarding and stance.
  • Black Stone shards (黑石碎片) - raise attack and poise-break (提升攻击和破势能力), the stat that breaks an enemy's guard.
  • Memory Flowers (记忆之花) - raise maximum health.

The effects are corroborated twice inside the wiki: the collectibles page and the combat-system page both state that health cap comes from Memory Flowers and Sha-chi bar cap from Sha-chi Amber, which is why this page lists them with confidence.

What is not known: the size of each gain. Earlier community write-ups circulated a flat +10% per pickup. Neither BWIKI revision behind this page nor any official material states a number, so the percentage has been removed from this page rather than repeated. Verify against the retail game before planning a farming route.

sections.title: Books and Story Items
sections.content:
Two further categories carry lore instead of power:

  • Books (书籍) - named volumes exist as collectible entries; the wiki lists 《"四凶斧"案卷》 ("The Four Axes" case file) with a chapter named 四凶斧之乱·祸乱. Readable lore rather than gear.
  • Story items (剧情道具) - objects that exist to move a quest or a location open. Two are documented: 浑源石, a cracked strange stone described as the power source of the Sha-chi transformation tower, and the 杀气炉探火孔开关, a control-panel switch for a viewing port on the lower level of the Sha-chi forging furnace.

Both story items are named in Chinese only, with no official English localisation published yet. Expect the retail names to differ.

sections.title: Bells Do Three Jobs
sections.content:
Bells (铃铛) are the backbone of the map system, and the reason collectibles and traversal are the same subject here:

  • Touching a bell for the first time clears the fog on the minimap around it - a bell is a map reveal, not just a waypoint.
  • Travel between bells is the game's fast travel. The 66 Days mode handles bells differently again: see difficulty modes.
  • Forced-combat waypoints are part of the same design - the wiki describes 强制战斗的战点设计, meaning some fight locks are built into the travel network rather than being optional detours.

Water travel (水面航行) also exists as an exploration method in at least one region.

sections.title: What Is Not a Collectible
sections.content:
Worth separating, because pre-launch lists on other sites blur these:

  • Weapons and Phantom Edges are equipment, tracked on their own pages (main weapons, Phantom Edges). Some are found in the world, and Phantom Edges are also obtained probabilistically, not only as pinned pickups.
  • Flasks and accessories are equipment slots - two flask slots and six accessory slots - rather than a completion category.
  • Remnant Spark, the resource Phantom Edges consume, drops probabilistically from kills. It is a currency, not something you collect once.

Terminology and structure on this page come from the 影之刃 WIKI on BWIKI - specifically the 收集要素 page (revision 3145, last edited 2026-10-13) and the 战斗系统 page, which independently confirm the same three item effects. That wiki is run by the moderators of the 影之刃 Baidu Tieba and states it has no affiliation with S-GAME. Anything below that is community-sourced rather than first-party is labelled as such, and no counts or percentages have been published before release.
